title: Unique universal n-term Nijenhuis-Richardson formulas for higher Koszul antibrackets over characteristic-zero commutative superalgebras
author: Marco Manetti; Giulia Ricciardi
source_title: Universal Lie Formulas for Higher Antibrackets
difficulty_reason: The proof realizes natural antibrackets as a module for a positive Witt algebra and establishes a triangular basis theorem for all arities. A polynomial-derivation test then eliminates the extra basis direction, producing the minimal n-term formula with rational coefficients. This universal all-arity construction exceeds verifying low-order Jacobi identities or expanding the definition of a bracket.
source_version: Official SIGMA 12 (2016) article 053, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2016.053; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.note: Full2.3 support in independent Section6 read: formal polynomial-operator model a, natural evaluation maps, the two explicit Witt representations and their Nijenhuis-Richardson module compatibility, basis induction through an invertible block-triangular matrix, and the nonzero polynomial-derivation test forcing b_n=0. The displayed shuffle identities give the bounded routine module checks and matrix entries. The proof is independent of the gauge-expansion2.1 and its iterative logarithm support. Coefficient uniqueness is universal for natural formulas across algebras/operators, as established in6.4; no assertion of linear independence after specializing to a single degenerate algebra/operator. The closed coefficient expression2.4 is conjectural and excluded.

statement_scope: For each n>=1, the universal natural higher Koszul bracket Phi_f^(n+1) on every characteristic-zero commutative superalgebra has the author unique rational coefficient formula c1*rho1^n(f)+sum(i=2..n)c_i*rho1^(n-i)rho_i(f), where rho_i=[mu_i,-] and mu_i multiplies i+1 arguments, with all Koszul signs and shuffle conventions as defined. Uniqueness is universal, not after specializing to an individual A or f. No conjectural closed formula2.4 or noncommutative extension is selected.

The full polynomial-operator natural-bracket model, both positive-Witt representations, module compatibility, block-triangular basis induction and polynomial-derivation test eliminating the extra direction are bundled as one universal all-arity outcome. Coefficient uniqueness is universal over all algebras/operators, as in the author model, rather than after one fixed specialization. Gauge-expansion Theorem 2.1 and iterative-logarithm support are not needed by this proof; conjectural closed coefficients and noncommutative extensions are unselected. The original repeated first term in the representation-commutator expansion and x/t notation in the derivation test are retained unchanged; the following author expansion is also included.
